h1:
Surat Thani in One Day
Town–Chaiya or Khao Sok
intro: Plenty of people pass through Surat Thani only to catch the ferry to Samui or Phangan, but if you've got a spare day, the place is more fun than you'd expect — no island hop required. We've split it into two routes so you can pick by mood and by how much time you have. The culture-and-food crowd heads to Town–Chaiya to pay respects at the thousand-year-old Phra Borommathat Chaiya stupa and pick up salted eggs, while the nature crowd makes a beeline for Khao Sok–Cheow Lan Lake for a longtail boat ride among limestone karsts that locals call the Guilin of Thailand.

blocks.html: Before you pick a route, ask yourself two things. One, do you have a car, and two, how early are you willing to wake up. The Town–Chaiya plan is the relaxed one — easy with your own car or a rental, short distances, and you're back in town in time for dinner. The Khao Sok plan means a serious early start, since the pier sits about 60 km from town, nearly two hours of driving. If you'd rather not drive, booking a day tour with transfers usually works out better.

blocks.text: Plan A — Town–Chaiya, for culture and food

blocks.html: This route suits anyone who wants to understand Surat Thani the way southern Thais live it. No need to wake up too early — Chaiya is about 50–55 km north of town, a little over an hour's drive, comfortable as a there-and-back day, and you'll still have time to come back and wander the evening market in town.

blocks.label: Plan A
blocks.title: Surat Thani town → Chaiya → back to town

items.activity: Start the morning with breakfast in Ban Don
items.note: Yok Kheng is a popular pick, with long tong (rice-noodle soup), pork satay, and dim sum from about 40–60 THB a plate. A mix of locals and visitors.
About 50–55 km, a little over an hour along Highway 41, smooth road the whole way.

items.activity: Pay respects at Phra Borommathat Chaiya, at Wat Phra Borommathat Chaiya Ratchaworawihan
items.note: The only genuine Srivijaya-era stupa in Thailand in this kind of condition, around a thousand years old. The temple also has a museum holding Srivijaya artifacts. No entry fee — dress modestly.

items.activity: On to Suan Mokkh (Wanachai Buddhist Monastery)
items.note: Buddhadasa's meditation retreat, just a few kilometers from the stupa. Walk through the Spiritual Theatre with its dharma-riddle murals, and the shaded forest. Quiet atmosphere, free entry.

items.activity: Lunch on local southern food around Chaiya
items.note: Several home-style spots sit out among the fields. Try gaeng tai pla (fish-organ curry), stir-fried stink beans, and khanom jeen with southern-style curry sauce.

items.activity: Stop by a Chaiya salted-egg community for souvenirs
items.note: Chaiya salted eggs are a GI product — deep-red yolks, rich but not overly salty, around 12–18 THB each. You can watch them being packed in termite-mound clay at the Lamet / Ban Songkhla communities.

items.activity: Drive back into Surat Thani town
items.note: A little over an hour, getting you back to town right around evening.

items.activity: Wrap up at San Chao Market, the downtown walking street
items.note: Open roughly 15:30–22:00. It's Ban Don's famous street-food spot along Ti Lek Road — graze your way through both savory and sweet.

blocks.title: Tip for Plan A
blocks.html: Phra Borommathat Chaiya and Suan Mokkh sit on opposite sides of the district but very close together, so pairing them in one morning is easy. If you don't have a car, there are vans and songthaews from town to Chaiya, but they don't run often — renting a car or chartering a taxi for half a day is more flexible.

blocks.text: Plan B — Khao Sok–Cheow Lan Lake, for nature

blocks.html: If you've come all the way to Surat Thani and want a view that sticks with you, Cheow Lan Lake (Ratchaprapha Dam) inside Khao Sok National Park is the answer. Sharp limestone peaks rise straight out of emerald-green water, which is how it earned the nickname the Guilin of Thailand. You really can do it as a day trip without staying overnight on a raft house, but you'll trade for an early start and a fair bit of time on the road.

blocks.label: Plan B
blocks.title: Town → dam pier → boat ride → back

items.note: The Ratchaprapha Dam pier is about 60 km from town, nearly 2 hours if you're driving. With a tour, a vehicle picks you up at your hotel.

items.activity: Arrive at the Ratchaprapha Dam pier and get ready to board
items.note: Pay the park fee first (a couple hundred THB for Thais). Chartering a whole longtail boat starts around 1,500–2,000 THB, or per-person with a tour from about 450–600 THB/person.

items.activity: Longtail ride to the Guilin of Thailand viewpoint (Khao Sam Kloe)
items.note: Three limestone peaks in the middle of emerald water — the lake's main photo spot. Cool, pleasant breeze in the morning.

items.activity: Stop at a floating restaurant and the fish-feeding spot
items.note: Big red-tailed barb gather here for the show. Some raft houses serve set lunches — steamed or stir-fried fish you can order.

items.activity: Short jungle walk, or visit Coral Cave / Diamond Cave
items.note: A roughly 1.5 km nature trail in the Khlong Saeng Wildlife Sanctuary, with a chance of spotting hornbills. The caves cost extra and depend on water levels.

items.activity: Boat back to the pier, last views along the way
items.note: The afternoon light shifts the water into a different, equally pretty shade.
You'll reach town by evening. Build in buffer time if you've got a ferry to the islands the next day.

blocks.title: Tip for Plan B
blocks.html: Water levels and weather decide whether you can enter the caves or do the jungle walk. Boats and tours often adjust the program on the spot for safety. Bring non-slip shoes, sun protection, and cash for the park fee, which usually isn't included in the package.

items: Half a day / no car → Plan A Town–Chaiya is more flexible and easy to trim down by time.
Want a nature view you'll remember → Plan B Khao Sok, but expect an early start and travel time.
Traveling with young kids or older folks → Plan A is easier, less walking, less sun.
Into photos and activities → Plan B gets you the boat ride, jungle walk, and caves all in one day.

blocks.text: Eats along the way you shouldn't skip

blocks.html: Whichever plan you pick, Surat Thani knows how to eat. Here's a shortlist of food you can actually stop for along the route, or before and after the trip.

items.name: Yok Kheng (Ban Don)
items.blurb: A legendary Surat Thani breakfast spot — long tong, pork satay, dim sum, and sweets. A great way to start the day before heading out.

items.name: San Chao Market (walking street)
items.blurb: The town's biggest evening street-food market, open roughly 15:30–22:00. Long rows of savory and sweet eats — a fitting end to Plan A.

items.name: Chaiya salted eggs (Lamet / Ban Songkhla)
items.blurb: A GI product with deep-red yolks, rich but not too salty. Good as a souvenir or eaten with rice porridge.

items.name: Local southern food around Chaiya
items.blurb: Gaeng tai pla, stir-fried stink beans with shrimp, khanom jeen with curry sauce — bold flavors the southern way, found at home-style spots out in the fields.

items.name: Khao Phra Ram Long Song, Lao O
items.blurb: A downtown institution of over 60 years — rice topped with blanched greens and a rich sesame sauce. An easy fill before or after the trip.

items.name: Steamed/fried fish set on a Cheow Lan raft
items.blurb: A lunch on a raft house mid boat ride — fresh fish straight from the lake, limestone peaks all around. Made for Plan B.

items.name: Surat Thani khao man kai
items.blurb: The town has several Hainanese chicken rice spots locals rate highly — fragrant rice and a punchy dipping sauce. A quick meal before hitting the road.

items.name: Sweets and coffee at San Chao Market
items.blurb: Cap things off with local sweets or old-style coffee at San Chao Market. Easy on the wallet, with plenty of stalls to graze.

blocks.text: More in-town spots if you've got time

items.name: Surat Thani City Pillar Shrine
items.blurb: On the Tapi River across from Sri Tapi Bridge, the city's guardian shrine. Open 07:00–19:00 — easy to drop in for a quick visit.

items.name: Tapi Riverside Walkway
items.blurb: A riverside path through the center of town. In the evening, locals come to exercise; good for photos of the bridge and river views.

items.name: Phra That Sri Surat (Khao Tha Phet)
items.blurb: A town viewpoint on a low hill you can drive up. Wide views over the town and the Tapi River.

faq.q: Where should I go in Surat Thani for one day without an island hop?
faq.a: There are two main routes. The Town–Chaiya route covers the thousand-year-old Phra Borommathat Chaiya stupa, Suan Mokkh, and Chaiya salted eggs — good for culture and food lovers. The other is Khao Sok–Cheow Lan Lake, a longtail boat ride past limestone peaks in emerald water — good for nature lovers.

faq.q: Can I do Cheow Lan Lake as a day trip from town?
faq.a: Yes, if you wake up early. The Ratchaprapha Dam pier is about 60 km from town, nearly 2 hours if you drive yourself, so leave town around 06:30 — or book a tour with transfers, which is easier. You'll be back in town by evening.

faq.q: About how much does the Cheow Lan Lake boat cost?
faq.a: Chartering a whole longtail boat starts around 1,500–2,000 THB, while per-person with a tour starts around 450–600 THB per person. That doesn't include the park fee or cave entry, which usually have to be paid separately on site.

faq.q: Can I visit Phra Borommathat Chaiya and Suan Mokkh together in one day?
faq.a: Easily. Both are in Chaiya district just a few kilometers apart, so they fit neatly into a morning. Follow up with a southern-food lunch and salted-egg shopping in the afternoon.

faq.q: Where do I buy Chaiya salted eggs, and how much are they?
faq.a: You can buy them at the salted-egg communities in Chaiya district, such as Lamet and Ban Songkhla. They're a GI product with deep-red yolks, around 12–18 THB each. Some places will show you how they're packed in termite-mound clay.
